concepts.name: Prior, likelihood, posterior
concepts.summary: Name and describe the prior, likelihood and posterior as the three parts of a Bayesian update.

concepts.name: Bayes' theorem for events
concepts.summary: Explain how Bayes' theorem reverses a conditional probability by combining P(B|A), P(A) and P(B).

concepts.name: Probability as degree of belief
concepts.summary: Explain that Bayesians use probability to express uncertainty about unknown quantities, not only long-run frequencies.

concepts.name: Parameters as random quantities
concepts.summary: Understand that an unknown parameter is described by a probability distribution that reflects what is currently known.

concepts.name: Updating beliefs with data
concepts.summary: Describe how a posterior after one batch of data can serve as the prior for the next.

concepts.name: Base rate and diagnostic reasoning
concepts.summary: Explain why a positive test result depends on the prevalence as well as sensitivity and specificity.

misconceptions.text: P(hypothesis | data) is the same as P(data | hypothesis).
A positive result from an accurate test means the condition is almost certainly present, regardless of how rare it is.
The prior is just a guess that the data will simply overwrite, so it does not matter.

concepts.name: Grid approximation of a posterior
concepts.summary: Compute a posterior for one parameter on a grid of values by multiplying prior and likelihood at each point and normalising.

concepts.name: Beta-binomial conjugate update
concepts.summary: Update a Beta prior with binomial data to obtain a Beta posterior by adding successes and failures.

concepts.name: Choosing a simple prior
concepts.summary: Pick a flat, weakly informative or informative prior for a proportion and justify the choice from context.

concepts.name: Credible interval
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret an interval that contains the parameter with stated posterior probability.

concepts.name: Posterior summaries
concepts.summary: Report posterior mean, median and mode (MAP) and say when they differ.

concepts.name: Prior strength as pseudo-observations
concepts.summary: Interpret prior parameters as equivalent prior data and see how sample size shifts weight toward the likelihood.

concepts.name: Posterior predictive for next observation
concepts.summary: Calculate the probability of a future outcome by averaging over the posterior in a simple model.

misconceptions.text: A 95% credible interval means that in 95% of repeated experiments the interval would cover the true value.
A flat prior is completely objective and adds no assumptions.
The posterior mean and the most likely value are always the same.

concepts.name: Conjugate families beyond beta-binomial
concepts.summary: Derive and apply conjugate updates for Poisson rates and normal means with known variance.

concepts.name: Prior sensitivity analysis
concepts.summary: Compare posteriors under different reasonable priors to judge how much conclusions depend on them.

concepts.name: Highest density intervals
concepts.summary: Distinguish equal-tailed from highest density intervals and choose between them for skewed posteriors.

concepts.name: Bayesian hypothesis comparison
concepts.summary: Compare two hypotheses using Bayes factors and posterior odds and analyse their sensitivity to priors.

concepts.name: Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling
concepts.summary: Explain and apply sampling from an unnormalised posterior with Metropolis-style algorithms.

concepts.name: Bayesian linear regression
concepts.summary: Specify priors on coefficients and noise, and interpret the resulting posterior over regression parameters.

concepts.name: MCMC convergence diagnostics
concepts.summary: Assess chains using trace plots, multiple chains, R-hat and effective sample size.

concepts.name: Posterior predictive checking
concepts.summary: Simulate data from the fitted model and compare to observed data to find misfit.

misconceptions.text: A Bayes factor is the probability that the hypothesis is true.
If the MCMC trace looks noisy and the run finished, the posterior samples are reliable.
With enough data prior sensitivity is irrelevant in every model.

concepts.name: Hierarchical models and partial pooling
concepts.summary: Analyse how group-level priors shrink group estimates and trade off between complete and no pooling.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo behaviour
concepts.summary: Analyse why gradient-based samplers scale better and diagnose divergences and poor geometry.

concepts.name: Model comparison with predictive criteria
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing models using cross-validated predictive performance and justify the selection.

concepts.name: Prior predictive checks for prior design
concepts.summary: Evaluate priors by simulating from the prior predictive distribution and judging plausibility.

concepts.name: Generalised linear models in Bayesian form
concepts.summary: Analyse Bayesian logistic and count models, including link functions and coefficient interpretation.

concepts.name: Decision-theoretic use of posteriors
concepts.summary: Evaluate actions by minimising posterior expected loss and justify the choice of loss.

concepts.name: Reparameterisation for sampling
concepts.summary: Analyse when reparameterising a model removes funnel-shaped posteriors and improves sampling.

misconceptions.text: Hierarchical models just average groups together and hide real differences between them.
The model with the best in-sample fit is the best model.
Divergent transitions in HMC can be ignored if R-hat looks fine.

concepts.name: Bayesian workflow design
concepts.summary: Design an iterative workflow of model building, fitting, checking and revision for a new problem.

concepts.name: Approximate inference trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate when variational or Laplace approximations are acceptable versus exact MCMC, and their known biases.

concepts.name: Nonparametric Bayesian models
concepts.summary: Construct flexible models with priors over functions or distributions for problems where parametric forms fail.

concepts.name: Simulation-based calibration
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether an inference procedure is correct by recovering parameters from simulated data.

concepts.name: Weak identifiability of parameters
concepts.summary: Judge when parameters are only weakly identified by the data and how much the prior then drives the posterior.

concepts.name: Latent-variable models for missing data and measurement error
concepts.summary: Build models that jointly handle missingness or measurement error by treating the true values as latent variables.

concepts.name: Communicating Bayesian results
concepts.summary: Critique and craft reports of posterior uncertainty, assumptions and decisions for non-specialist stakeholders.

misconceptions.text: Variational inference gives the same posterior as MCMC, only faster.
If the sampler converges, the model must be a good description of reality.
Nonparametric Bayesian models have no assumptions because they have no fixed parameters.
